LESSON: CREATION OF PLANTS AND ANIMALS

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Family learner should be able to: family of your nuclear family? Creation 6 less
Topic 1.3: Creation of Plants and Animals

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Creation of Plants and Animals. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do you take part of the environment ● Learners to draw and colour some plants that care of plants?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify common animals found at home, school, and in Kenya
2. group animals in simple ways (for example domestic and wild, or those that live on land and in water)
3. describe how selected animals move, feed, or protect themselves
4. practise kind and safe care for animals

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CREATION OF PLANTS AND ANIMALS
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Creation of Plants and Animals helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS ABOUT ANIMALS
Animals are living things. They move, feed, grow, and respond to their surroundings.
Domestic animals live with people (cow, goat, chicken, dog, cat).
Wild animals live on their own in forests, parks, or water (lion, zebra, fish).
In Kenya you may see cows in a homestead, fish at a market, or birds on the school field.
Safety: do not touch unknown animals; wash hands after handling pets or farm animals.

PART 1: Identify common animals found at home, school, and in Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to identify common animals found at home, school, and in Kenya. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify common animals found at home, school, and in Kenya.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Creation of Plants and Animals” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify common animals found at home, school, and in Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Group animals in simple ways (for example domestic and wild, or those that live on land and in water)

What this means
In this part you learn to group animals in simple ways (for example domestic and wild, or those that live on land and in water). You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: group animals in simple ways (for example domestic and wild, or those that live on land and in water).
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Creation of Plants and Animals matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can group animals in simple ways (for example domestic and wild, or those that live on land and in water). Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Describe how selected animals move, feed, or protect themselves

What this means
In this part you learn to describe how selected animals move, feed, or protect themselves. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe how selected animals move, feed, or protect themselves.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Creation of Plants and Animals this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe how selected animals move, feed, or protect themselves. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Practise kind and safe care for animals

What this means
In this part you learn to practise kind and safe care for animals. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise kind and safe care for animals.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Creation of Plants and Animals” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise kind and safe care for animals. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Creation of Plants and Animals is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Domestic animals live with people (cow, goat, chicken, dog, cat).

Wild animals live on their own in forests, parks, or water (lion, zebra, fish).

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Creation of Plants and Animals” around your school. (skill: identify common animals found at home, school, and in Kenya)

Example 2: Say why Creation of Plants and Animals matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: group animals in simple ways (for example domestic and wild, or those that live on land and in water))

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Creation of Plants and Animals this week. (skill: describe how selected animals move, feed, or protect themselves)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Creation of Plants and Animals” around your school. (skill: practise kind and safe care for animals)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Creation of Plants and Animals to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify common animals found at home, school, and in Kenya.
3. Practise this skill: group animals in simple ways (for example domestic and wild, or those that live on land and in water).
4. Practise this skill: describe how selected animals move, feed, or protect themselves.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Creation of Plants and Animals from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Creation of Plants and Animals: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Creation of Plants and Animals?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do you take part of the environment ● Learners to draw and colour some plants that care of plants?
2. Why do you take part of God’s creation. ● Learners to give reasons for taking care of care of animals?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Creation of Plants and Animals means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify common animals found at home, school, and in Kenya.
5. Be able to: group animals in simple ways (for example domestic and wild, or those that live on land and in water).

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
